newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent trades up, other grades go quietly.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent trades up, other grades go quietly.

text.p: North Sea Brent differentials and paper markets firmed on Wednesday despite a drop in outright prices, traders said.

Good buying of short-term swaps for July 14-18 brought levels up in an otherwise bearish market, with a Brent cargo trading 5 cents higher, as buyers emerged to sweep barrels off the tight physical scene.

The market is still underpinned by absent Iraqi barrels, which pushed buyers to meet July needs promptly, even though news Baghdad could be closer to resuming exports and bearish stock data knocked IPE futures down some 30 cents to around $18.10 a barrel.
Deals were being done quietly on Wednesday after Tuesday's flurry of activity, with solid numbers believed paid in a number of confidential deals for non-Brent North Sea grades.
A Forties cargo loading July 25-27 went for 40 cents over dated Brent to the same buyer who paid two cents under flat for a July 26-28 Gullfaks A on Tuesday.
Oseberg barrels may also have changed hands, with speculation they would follow same grade cargoes traded earlier in the week to the Mediterranean, where Russian Urals is scarce and expensive.
"It looks like the market is still quite tight on the grades and avails for July are getting thinner and thinner," said a trader.
The July 21-23 Brent traded on Wednesday at August Brent +10 cents was believed bound for the U.S. Gulf aboard a ULCC.

The buyer also kept the cargo that turned wet on Wednesday, which loads July 24-26, and now holds at least five parcels, if rumours prove true that he managed to take 1 million barrels loading July 22-24, on a dated related basis.
Reports that the Brent July 23-25 loader also traded to the same buyer could not be confirmed.
The activity boosted next week's (July 14-18) contracts for differences from Sept -25 cents when the day began to around -12 cents, having traded at -20 and -17 cents.
Weeks further out were also pushed up, with July 21-25 bid up from -23 cents to -18 cents.
Intermonth spreads firmed, with July/August talked up from +22/25 to +25/35, while Aug/Sept traded at -8, -7 and -6 cents.

"The physical has been quite strong and with the Iraq situation people had held off on Friday and Monday so things started to move yesterday and today," said one broker. "Nothing really came out of Baghdad today but at least it was not bad news."
Russian Urals values were still held strong by the 300,000 tonne Turkish sour crude buy tender, which has paralysed all trade.
West African trade was steady and balanced with a South Korean refinery confirmed having bought on Tuesday a VLCC combo cargo of Nembe/Cabinda/Palanca, loading 12-15 August.
The Cabinda element was heard priced at $1.10 below dated Brent, the Nembe a few cents above flat and the Palanca in the high 20s.
